faqs.question: Should a Tamil love letter be in literary Tamil or spoken Tamil?
faqs.answer: Spoken Tamil. Tamil is diglossic, and Harold Schiffman's 1998 Language in Society paper notes that Literary Tamil "is never used for informal oral communication between live speakers" — so a letter in it reads like an exam answer. The IruMozhi study found only 2.0% of sentences in a 15,744-comment Tamil YouTube corpus classify as Literary Tamil.

faqs.question: Should I call her நீ or நீங்க in a Tamil love letter?
faqs.answer: நீ if you are already together; நீங்க for a first letter to someone who has not said yes. நீ assumes a closeness she has not agreed to yet, and the verb ending has to follow the pronoun you pick — நீ வர்றியா against நீங்க வர்றீங்களா.

faqs.question: What if my girlfriend speaks Tamil but cannot read Tamil script?
faqs.answer: Send the same spoken Tamil in Roman letters. That is not a compromise — the IruMozhi authors note Spoken Tamil is largely found in the Latin script online, and the Dakshina dataset exists because 12 South Asian languages are routinely written that way.

faqs.question: How do I type Tamil on WhatsApp or Instagram?
faqs.answer: Both iOS and Android ship a Tamil keyboard you add once in language or keyboard settings, after which Tamil sends as normal Unicode text. If you would rather not set that up, type the romanised version — it needs no extra keyboard and she can reply on the one already open.

faqs.question: How long should a love letter in Tamil be?
faqs.answer: Shorter than you think. Every letter in this post is three to five sentences, because a long letter in a second register is where stilted phrasing creeps in. One specific detail — a voice note played three times, a Tuesday afternoon — carries more than a paragraph of adjectives.

faqs.question: Is it a good idea to quote Thirukkural or classical Tamil poetry in a love letter?
faqs.answer: One line, at most, and only if she likes that register. A Kural is literary Tamil by definition, so it sits in a different register from the rest of your letter and can read as borrowed rather than felt. If you use one, keep the surrounding letter in spoken Tamil so the quote is clearly a quote.

faqs.question: What is a very short love letter in Tamil I can put in a locket or a status?
faqs.answer: நான் அதிகமா பேசுறவன் இல்லை. அதனால ஒரு வரி மட்டும்: நீ இருக்கிற இடம் தான் எனக்கு வீடு. Romanised: Naan adhigamaa pesuravan illai. Adhanaala oru vari mattum: nee irukkira idam thaan enakku veedu. It means: I am not one for talking much, so one line — wherever you are is home to me.

faqs.question: Does Sri Lankan Tamil change how I should write the letter?
faqs.answer: Yes, enough to matter. Schiffman's work notes the Indian and Sri Lankan Tamil dialects are extremely divergent, and spoken forms vary by region and community even within Tamil Nadu. Write in the spoken Tamil of her household rather than the film-dialogue koiné if the two differ.

faqs.question: Is a handwritten Tamil letter better than sending a link?
faqs.answer: Handwriting wins when you can hand it over. Across cities it loses to a link, and 50.3% of SubhSandesh page views happen on a phone — a page can also be password-protected, which 42.9% of creators here do before sharing.

faqs.question: Which Tamil phrase for "I love you" should I actually use?
faqs.answer: உன்னை நான் காதலிக்கிறேன் is correct and formal; உன்னைப் பிடிக்கும் is what people say. In a spoken-register letter the plainer form lands harder, and lines like நீ இல்லாம முடியல do more work than the textbook sentence.

faqs.question: How do I make a Tamil letter I found online not read as copy-paste?
faqs.answer: Change three things: the pronoun to the one that matches your actual relationship, the register from literary to spoken, and at least one detail only the two of you know. The median SubhSandesh creator spends 6.9 hours between first save and last edit on an "I love you" page, which is mostly this kind of rewriting.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Love Letter for Girlfriend in Tamil: Write It in Spoken Tamil

Write your love letter in Tamil in spoken Tamil — கொடுந்தமிழ், the register you actually talk in — not the literary Tamil of school textbooks, and put a romanised version beside the Tamil script so she can read it without a Tamil keyboard.

The "I love you" page is the most-created thing on SubhSandesh: 975 pages, 29.2% of everything built here since 2026-03-12. Its median gap between first save and last edit is 6.9 hours across all 975 — what rewriting a love letter all afternoon looks like in data.

Below: six complete letters in Tamil script, romanisation and English, the நீ / நீங்க decision nobody explains, and what diglossia research says about why a formal letter reads like homework.

## Why literary Tamil reads like a school essay and spoken Tamil reads like a person

Tamil is diglossic: two varieties in everyday use at once. Literary Tamil is preferred in writing and formal communication; Spoken Tamil is confined to speech and informal media.

Harold Schiffman of the University of Pennsylvania puts it flatly in his 1998 *Language in Society* paper on [Standard Spoken Tamil](https://ccat.sas.upenn.edu/~haroldfs/public/stantam/STANTAM.HTM): Literary Tamil "is never used for informal oral communication between live speakers."

The written standard she was taught was codified by the grammarian Pavaṇanti in the thirteenth century. That is the register a Tamil exam answer is marked in, and the register almost every ready-made Tamil love letter online uses.

The gap is measurable. [IruMozhi](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07804), a 2023 study that trained classifiers on parallel Literary and Spoken Tamil, then audited real Tamil corpora: only 2.0% of sentences in a [15,744-comment Tamil YouTube corpus](https://aclanthology.org/2020.sltu-1.28/) classified as Literary Tamil.

அன்புள்ள and உன்னை நான் காதலிக்கிறேன் are correct Tamil. உன்னைப் பிடிக்கும் and நீ இல்லாம முடியல are how you would actually say it.

## நீ or நீங்க: the one word that sets the temperature

Tamil has two second-person pronouns, and choosing is a social decision rather than a grammatical one. நீ is singular and intimate. நீங்க is the plural form used to one person, carrying deference or distance.

For a girlfriend of some years, நீ. For a first letter to someone who has not said yes, நீங்க — நீ before she has agreed to that closeness reads as presumption.

No page currently ranking for this search names the choice; they hand over the intimate form by default, including in first-confession letters. The pronoun drags the verb with it, as Schiffman's spoken-Tamil grammar sets out: நீ வர்றியா against நீங்க வர்றீங்களா. Pick one in the first line and do not drift; drifting mid-letter is the clearest sign a letter was assembled rather than written.

## Six love letters for your girlfriend in Tamil, ordered by register

Ordered by how much each letter has to carry, not by occasion: the first must not presume, the last is the hardest to get right. Each is short and in spoken Tamil, with the same fields — when to use it, which pronoun, the Tamil, the romanisation, the English sense.

### 1. நீங்க, before there is a "we"


**Use when:** you have not told her. **Register:** நீங்க.

**Tamil:** ரொம்ப நாளா இதை எழுதணும்னு நினைச்சேன், தைரியம் வரலை. நீங்க பேசுறதைக் கேட்டுக்கிட்டே இருக்கலாம்னு தோணும். அது நட்பு மட்டும் இல்லைன்னு எனக்கு இப்போ புரியுது. உங்களுக்கு எப்படி இருக்கோ தெரியாது. பதில் என்னவா இருந்தாலும் சரி, நான் மாறமாட்டேன்.

**Roman:** Romba naalaa idhai ezhudhanum-nu ninaichen, dhairiyam varala. Neenga pesuradhaik kettukkitte irukkalaam-nu thonum. Adhu natpu mattum illai-nu enakku ippo puriyudhu. Ungalukku eppadi irukko theriyaadhu. Badhil ennavaa irundhaalum sari, naan maara maatten.

**English:** I have wanted to write this for a long time and never had the nerve. When you talk, I could just keep listening. I understand now it is not only friendship. I do not know how it is for you. Whatever your answer, I will not change.

### 2. நீ with no occasion behind it


**Use when:** nothing happened, which is the point. **Register:** நீ.

**Tamil:** காரணம் ஒண்ணும் இல்லை. செவ்வாய்க்கிழமை, மூணு மணி, ஆபீஸ்ல உட்கார்ந்திருக்கேன். உன் பேரு நினைவுக்கு வந்துச்சு, அதனால எழுதுறேன். அது தான் விஷயம். சாயந்திரம் சாப்பிட்டியான்னு கேட்பேன். நீ இல்லைன்னு சொல்லுவ, தெரியும்.

**Roman:** Kaaranam onnum illai. Sevvaaikkizhamai, moonu mani, office-la utkaarndhirukken. Un peru ninaivukku vandhuchu, adhanaala ezhudhuren. Adhu thaan vishayam. Saayandhiram saappittiyaa-nu kekpen. Nee illai-nu solluva, theriyum.

**English:** No reason. Tuesday, three o'clock, sitting at the office. Your name came into my head, so I am writing. That is all. Tonight I will ask whether you ate. You will say no. I know.

### 3. நீ at its shortest


**Use when:** a book note, a locket, a status. **Register:** நீ.

**Tamil:** நான் அதிகமா பேசுறவன் இல்லை. அதனால ஒரு வரி மட்டும்: நீ இருக்கிற இடம் தான் எனக்கு வீடு.

**Roman:** Naan adhigamaa pesuravan illai. Adhanaala oru vari mattum: nee irukkira idam thaan enakku veedu.

**English:** I am not one for talking much. So, one line: wherever you are is home to me.

### 4. நீ across two cities


**Use when:** different cities, calls sounding like admin. **Register:** நீ.

**Tamil:** இன்னைக்கு ஒரு மாசம் ஆயிடுச்சு உன்னைப் பார்க்காம. காலைல எழுந்திரிச்சு ஃபோன் பார்க்கிறது பழக்கமாயிடுச்சு. நீ அனுப்புன ஒரு வாய்ஸ் நோட்டை மூணு தடவ கேட்டேன். அடுத்த மாசம் வர்றேன். அது வரைக்கும் நான் இங்கே இருக்கேன், ஆனா முழுசா இல்லை.

**Roman:** Innaikku oru maasam aayiduchu unnaip paakkaama. Kaalaila ezhundhirichu phone paakkiradhu pazhakkam aayiduchu. Nee anuppuna oru voice note-a moonu thadava ketten. Adutha maasam varren. Adhu varaikkum naan inge irukken, aana muzhusaa illai.

**English:** A month today since I saw you. Waking up and checking my phone has become a habit. I played one voice note you sent three times over. I come next month. Until then I am here, but not all of me.

### 5. நீ on a day she expects something


**Use when:** it is her birthday and you want more than a forwarded graphic. **Register:** நீ.

**Tamil:** பிறந்தநாள் வாழ்த்துக்கள். இது நாலாவது வருஷம் நான் உனக்கு இதைச் சொல்றது. ஒவ்வொரு வருஷமும் நீ கொஞ்சம் தைரியமாகிட்டே போற. அதைப் பார்க்கிறது எனக்கு பிடிக்கும். இந்த வருஷம் பெரிசா எதுவும் கேட்கல. நீ சந்தோஷமா இரு, அது போதும்.

**Roman:** Pirandhanaal vaazhthukkal. Idhu naalaavadhu varusham naan unakku idhaich solradhu. Ovvoru varushamum nee konjam dhairiyamaagitte pora. Adhaip paakkiradhu enakku pidikkum. Indha varusham perisaa edhuvum kekkala. Nee sandhoshamaa iru, adhu podhum.

**English:** Happy birthday. Fourth year I am saying this to you. Every year you get a little braver, and I like watching it happen. I am not asking for anything big. Just be happy — that is enough.

### 6. நீ when you were wrong


**Use when:** you were wrong and a call would restart it. **Register:** நீ.

**Tamil:** நேத்து நான் பேசுன விதம் தப்பு. அதுக்கு காரணம் சொல்ல மாட்டேன், அது சாக்கு ஆயிடும். உன் பக்கம் சரியா இருந்ததுன்னு இப்போ புரியுது. கேட்காம பேசிட்டேன். கோபம் போற வரைக்கும் காத்திருக்கேன். ஃபோன் வேண்டாம், நேரா பேசலாம்.

**Roman:** Nethu naan pesuna vidham thappu. Adhukku kaaranam solla maatten, adhu saakku aayidum. Un pakkam sariyaa irundhadhu-nu ippo puriyudhu. Kekkaama pesitten. Kobam pora varaikkum kaathirukken. Phone vendaam, neraa pesalaam.

**English:** The way I spoke yesterday was wrong. I will not give a reason, because that would be an excuse. Your side was right. I talked without listening. I will wait until the anger passes. No call — let us talk face to face.

If the register you want is heavier than any of these — the cinematic, dark-romantic one Tamil film dialogue trades in — the [dark, dramatic romantic page for a partner](https://subhsandesh.in/darling) carries that mood without forcing it into the words.

## Tamil script, romanised Tamil or English: which one she can actually read

Romanised Indic text is not a shortcut somebody invented. The [Dakshina dataset](https://aclanthology.org/2020.lrec-1.294/), released at LREC 2020, exists because 12 South Asian languages are routinely written in the Latin script too. IruMozhi's authors say the same of Tamil: Spoken Tamil is largely found in the Latin script online.

| Option | Keyboard she needs to reply in kind | Register it carries | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tamil script | A Tamil keyboard, added by hand in iOS or Android settings | Her own script; a Tamil reader takes it as effort spent | A handwritten letter, or a page she reads rather than types back into — 50.3% of SubhSandesh views are on a phone, where the reply keyboard is the friction |
| Romanised spoken Tamil | None; the English keyboard already open | Exactly how you would say it aloud, and the form that 15,744-comment Tamil corpus is written in | WhatsApp and Instagram; anyone Tamil-speaking but English-schooled |
| English translation | None | Correct meaning, visibly less specific — நீ இருக்கிற இடம் தான் எனக்கு வீடு flattens to "you are my home" | A girlfriend who does not read Tamil at all |

For most people the answer is both: Tamil script first, romanisation under it. The [DravidianCodeMix corpus](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388449/), published in *Language Resources and Evaluation* in 2022 with around 44,000 Tamil-English comments, counted a comment as Tamil whether it arrived in Tamil or Latin script.

## Where to put the letter so the Tamil survives the send

Tamil script pasted into a chat thread competes with notifications, and a chat message cannot be password-protected. That is why 42.9% of SubhSandesh creators — 1,432 of 3,335 — lock their page before sharing it, and why 99.5% of started pages get published.

A [romantic "I love you" page for a girlfriend](https://subhsandesh.in/love-gf) holds the Tamil script, the romanisation and the English gloss as three stacked blocks on one page, with a gallery, music and an optional password. It is also the most-viewed template here — 14,396 views, 35.2% of all 40,864 recorded views — which mostly means these pages get re-opened rather than read once.

That 6.9-hour median between first save and last edit is not indecision. It is people going back to fix one line, and register is exactly that kind of line.

## When a Tamil letter is the wrong choice

If she reads Tamil slowly — common for Tamil speakers schooled entirely in English — a Tamil-script letter becomes a comprehension exercise, and she will be decoding when you wanted her moved. Send romanised Tamil.

If you are in the same room, say it out loud. A letter is a distance technology, which is why it works across cities and badly across a sofa.

And if her family reads it over her shoulder — real in plenty of Tamil households — the intimate நீ in Tamil script is louder than the same sentiment in English. Pick the register for the actual audience.

## Sources

- Schiffman, ["Standardization or Restandardization: the case for 'Standard' Spoken Tamil"](https://ccat.sas.upenn.edu/~haroldfs/public/stantam/STANTAM.HTM), *Language in Society* 27(3), 1998
- Prasanna and Arora, [IruMozhi: Automatically classifying diglossia in Tamil](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07804), 13 November 2023
- Chakravarthi et al., [Corpus Creation for Sentiment Analysis in Code-Mixed Tamil-English Text](https://aclanthology.org/2020.sltu-1.28/), SLTU-CCURL 2020
- Chakravarthi et al., [DravidianCodeMix](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388449/), *Language Resources and Evaluation*, 2022
- Roark et al., [Processing South Asian Languages Written in the Latin Script: the Dakshina Dataset](https://aclanthology.org/2020.lrec-1.294/), LREC 2020, covering 12 languages

failed.why: metaTitle is 60 characters — inside the 50–60 target and well inside the 70 cap — with one separator, and the target keyword starts at word one; but the keyword "love letter for girlfriend in tamil" is six words long, so it cannot sit wholly inside the first five words. Position one is the strongest placement available. I tested whether the 62–70 band buys a real differentiator, measuring Arial 20px pixel width against Google's ~580px desktop title truncation rather than character count, and it does not. Tested and rejected: "— 6 Spoken-Tamil Letters, Romanised" (71 chars / 641px) and ": 6 Spoken-Tamil Letters, Dual Script" (72 / 618px) breach the Strapi cap and truncate; "— 6 Letters, Script + Romanised" (67 / 586px), "— Spoken Tamil, Not Book Tamil" (66 / 592px) and "— 6 Letters, நீ or நீங்க Marked" (67 / 599px) each truncate exactly on the differentiator they add, which is the failure mode meta-and-titles.md warns about; ": 6 Letters in Spoken Tamil" (62 / 529px) leaves the target band for the identical claim at identical width; "— 6 Letters, Both Scripts" (61 / 519px) is a vaguer differentiator; "— 6 Letters in நீ or நீங்க" (62 / 543px) fits, and the pronoun is the thing no competitor has, but it trades away the spoken-register claim that is the post's whole angle for two glyphs a searcher who has not read the page cannot decode; "6 Love Letters for Girlfriend in Tamil — Spoken, Not Book Tamil" (63 / 565px) fits but pluralises "Letters", destroying exact match and breaking the keyword item. auditReport.honestAssessment: The Tamil in all six letters is non-native composition and must get a native Tamil read-through before this publishes. Three lines I specifically doubt, by the letters' new numbering: in letter 1 (நீங்க, before there is a "we"), "நீங்க பேசுறதைக் கேட்டுக்கிட்டே இருக்கலாம்னு தோணும்" — the -ன்னு தோணும் frame is right but the clause may read clipped, and it is the one place a நீங்க/நீ register leak could hide; in the same letter, "உங்களுக்கு எப்படி இருக்கோ தெரியாது" may not idiomatically carry "I do not know how you feel"; and in letter 2 (நீ with no occasion behind it), "சாயந்திரம் சாப்பிட்டியான்னு கேட்பேன்", where the quotative -ஆன்னு on a past-tense question is the exact construction that came out ungrammatical in the previous batch, and where the English gloss says "tonight" while the Tamil sets the asking at சாயந்திரம், evening. In that same letter I corrected a romanisation this pass: உட்கார்ந்திருக்கேன் was romanised "utkaandhirukken", now "utkaarndhirukken". A native writer would most likely reduce the Tamil itself to the colloquial உக்காந்திருக்கேன், which would also serve the post's spoken-register argument better — I have not made that change, because guessing at Tamil is precisely what the native gate exists to prevent. I am not a substitute for a native reader, and none of these three flags is resolved. The competitor-structure item closed on first-hand evidence this pass. I fetched the heading structures of the five pages ranking for this query: four carry no editorial structure at all — a translation-memory page of alternating English/Tamil rows, a blogspot kavithai whose only headings are blog furniture, a site-navigation H2 stack over one unsectioned letter, and an image grid with a single H1 — while the one article-shaped page is a flat occasion catalogue (first confession, apology, long distance, anniversary, birthday, gratitude, encouragement, getaway, good morning, tough times, each H2 suffixed with the keyword, then a conclusion). Four of this post's six letter H3s had been keyed to the same occasion buckets in nearly the same order, so all six are now keyed to the register ladder the two preceding H2s set up and reordered by how much each letter has to carry, with the occasions moved into the Use-when lines. That deliberately costs some occasion-phrase relevance in the headings. On why an answer engine would cite this over those five: it is the only page on this query that names Tamil diglossia as the problem and sources it (Schiffman 1998; IruMozhi's 2.0% Literary-Tamil estimate over a 15,744-comment corpus), the only one that explains நீ versus நீங்க — none of the five mentions the choice, and the one article-shaped page uses the intimate form in both of its first-confession samples — and the only one giving every letter in Tamil script plus romanisation plus English. Against that: subhsandesh.in has far less authority than the image-grid and social-discover pages holding these positions, the query is a small 300–1,000/mo estimate, and Tamil-language relevance signals for an English-language query are weak. The remaining metaTitle item is arithmetically unclosable, not unfixed. Ranking takes months and is not predicted here.
